video_title: Kwame Brown Talks Lebron James, Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and his Life | FULL INTERVIEW

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his time playing with Allen Iverson in Detroit
quotes.excerpt: I played with the greatest little man in the game too, Allen Iverson.
quotes.quote: I played with the greatest little man in the game too, Allen Iverson. He played up in Detroit one season with the Detroit Pistons. It was a tough situation for him because he didn't want to leave Denver and the Detroit Pistons were so tight with Chauncey Billups.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on being bused to a predominantly white school
quotes.excerpt: I was exposed to school choice where they bused me from a small neighborhood to a predominantly white school.
quotes.quote: I was exposed to school choice where they bused me from a small neighborhood to a predominantly white school. That opened up my eyes to a whole different life that was outside of my little two or three block radius before. I was just a guy who dreamed bigger than my situation.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the NBA's focus on women and media narratives
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is more about women, women, women.
quotes.quote: The NBA is more about women, women, women. I was the first overall draft pick, and they came to my mother and tried to get her to do a bunch of interviews to bash my father. She never bashed my father to me because she didn't want my mind caught up in that. I learned then about this business that if you don't give the story, somebody will tell it for you.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his high school development and academic struggles
quotes.excerpt: I got serious about my grades because I got in trouble and I had to get going on my grades.
quotes.quote: I got serious about my grades because I got in trouble and I had to get going on my grades. There was too much freedom in high school. I was used to more structure at the other school. In high school, you get to walk across the street for class and all that, and I was like, forget that, I'm going to the gym. I got caught doing that, so I had to make up those classes.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on realizing he could be the number one draft pick
quotes.excerpt: When the news reports came out about Tyson Chandler could be the number one pick or Eddie Curry could be the number one pick.
quotes.quote: When the news reports came out about Tyson Chandler could be the number one pick or Eddie Curry could be the number one pick, I'm like, wait a minute, I played against those two. I won MVP of that tournament and I played against Tyson and Eddie and I was like, if they're slated to be the number one pick, I did great against both of them, so I might as well throw my hat in the bucket and see what happens.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the Washington Wizards' failed three-way trade
quotes.excerpt: Chicago wanted to trade Tyson Chandler to the Clippers and wanted to trade Elton Brand to the Bulls.
quotes.quote: Chicago wanted to trade Tyson Chandler to the Clippers and wanted to trade Elton Brand to the Bulls. It was supposed to be a three-way trade and Elton Brand was supposed to go to the Bulls because MJ didn't believe in playing with unproven players. He brought in North Carolina guys, he brought in Stackhouse, he brought in Juwan Howard. He wanted to bring in Elton Brand, and then hopefully he was going to get enough pieces with Stack to win a championship, or at least get to the playoffs. So Abe Pollin really screwed up everything because Abe Pollin didn't want to trade away a number one pick because of what happened with Rasheed and all these other guys that he had drafted number one, Juwan Howard. He had drafted so many good players that as soon as they leave Washington, their career blossoms. So he decided to hold on to me.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his conflict with Stackhouse in Washington
quotes.excerpt: Stackhouse one day told him, I didn't come here to be your Scottie Pippen.
quotes.quote: Stackhouse one day told him, I didn't come here to be your Scottie Pippen. He thought that he was going to be the number one option and then MJ would be backing him up, but he found out very quickly that that wasn't the case and MJ was the number one option and Stack had to get in where he fit in.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his one-on-one battles with Tyson Chandler
quotes.excerpt: Me and Tyson didn't get to play against each other as much because they had other guys there, but I was scoring on everybody.
quotes.quote: Me and Tyson didn't get to play against each other as much because they had other guys there, but I was scoring on everybody. Tyson was off the charts far as everything athletic. I think he won every drill besides I think like the speed drill, I think I got him on that, but that was about it far as the height, far as some of the agility stuff. He was one of the most athletic dudes there.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on Michael Jordan's coaching style and trash talk
quotes.excerpt: He's one of the biggest guys that's going to talk trash.
quotes.quote: He's one of the biggest guys that's going to talk trash. And the crazy thing is, at 19, I started the trash talking with him. I wanted to play him one-on-one. I'm like, man, I don't think he that good. This is this and that. You the old man, you know, I'm just 19, that's what a 19-year-old is going to do. So he finally played me one-on-one and he cheated by the way, so I kept saying he cheated. I kept talking trash to him. We had a playful, I would make him, he would get tired of me so much so the smack in the back of the head thing that everybody always talking about, I mess around and was playing with Michael Jordan because I would always mess with him.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the media's misrepresentation of his career
quotes.excerpt: I feel bad for the Andrew Wiggins and people that didn't really get a chance to get the ball.
quotes.quote: I feel bad for the Andrew Wiggins and people that didn't really get a chance to get the ball and be that number one, and then if you're not good enough, hey, you take the, you take how it come and that's life. But at the end of the day, to not have your boss come downstairs and play with you and letting you know that I'm still your boss, and he's the number one icon that's ever played the game and they're running everything through him and he's wanting pieces and not you, so I had to endure not being wanted on the team.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the media circus surrounding Michael Jordan's return
quotes.excerpt: We went from two cameras to the entire NBA in the hallways.
quotes.quote: We went from two cameras to the entire NBA in the hallways. Shoot, that's a major difference right there, especially on the Wizards and Mike's coming back, that's that's huge.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the media's unfair portrayal of his family
quotes.excerpt: I knew what Chris Whitney said, I knew what Jahidi White said, and they stressed that media misrepresented you as a person.
quotes.quote: I knew what Chris Whitney said, I knew what Jahidi White said, and they stressed that media misrepresented you as a person and that you were intelligent, mature for your age. And they didn't show you like that. They showed you as an immature kid that can't really do anything for himself.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the NBA's treatment of players and their families
quotes.excerpt: The NBA, that should be a shame on the NBA for them to allow stories to be ran like that.
quotes.quote: The NBA, that should be a shame on the NBA for them to allow stories to be ran like that. They vetted myself and my whole family. So for them to just allow people to put out articles that they give away $12 million to teenagers that's not ready for that type of money or that's not mature enough for that type of money, that says a lot about them. That mean they should have fired everybody.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his relationship with Michael Jordan
quotes.excerpt: MJ, like they, they never picked me to keep me for the Washington Wizards.
quotes.quote: MJ, like they, they never picked me to keep me for the Washington Wizards. And that's what people don't understand. Chicago wanted to trade Tyson Chandler to the Clippers and wanted to trade Elton Brand to the Bulls, and they eventually did do that trade, but they wanted to trade Tyson to the Clippers and they wanted to bring in Elton Brand. And MJ didn't believe in playing with unproven players. So just imagine, MJ is the type of guy, if he's going to play, he wants to try to get to the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his role as a center and his physical limitations
quotes.excerpt: They wanted to play me at center but my knees were hurting was hurting too bad at the beginning of the season.
quotes.quote: They wanted to play me at center but my knees were hurting was hurting too bad at the beginning of the season. I went from guard to they wanted to play me at center, but my knees were hurting was hurting too bad at the beginning of the season.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his experience with different coaching styles
quotes.excerpt: The coach was asking me, what side of the court do you like the ball on?
quotes.quote: The coach was asking me, what side of the court do you like the ball on? What areas do you like to score? And that's how I'm like, I like this place, I like being on the right side, I like, like I'm getting to tell him what I like. I'm able to turn and face and go and have room to operate. And then, who wants to see a 19-year-old with the ball when MJ says he's coming back downstairs and he hadn't played basketball at how many years? So that wasn't happening. And he brought in North Carolina guys, he brought in Stackhouse, he brought in Juwan Howard. He wanted to bring in Elton Brand, and then hopefully he was going to get enough pieces with Stack to win a championship, or at least get to the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the importance of reputation in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: If you ever make it to the league, be careful of how you package your reputation.
quotes.quote: If you ever make it to the league, be careful of how you package your reputation. The things that they're going to place things on you like they do Jaylen Brown for no reason. But if you, if you mess up your reputation and they label you something, you're going to have to fight and scratch and become a whole different player just to stay in the league.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on his time with the Lakers and Phil Jackson
quotes.excerpt: Phil Jackson was a master at breaking down that triangle.
quotes.quote: Phil Jackson was a master at breaking down that triangle. And if you wanted to come in extra, he always had somebody available for you. So you didn't have to come in, they ain't going to beat your body up. You work on basketball movements, they always had three or four guys around for you to work on the triangle. And once I got that down and knew all the cuts, I loved it. I loved LA. It was good.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kwame Brown on the importance of player development and coaching
quotes.excerpt: I learned from him, they're able to get college jobs, they're able to get high school jobs based on that.
quotes.quote: I learned from him, they're able to get college jobs, they're able to get high school jobs based on that. They're able to say, I sat on the bench next to Kobe, I learned from him. They're able to get college jobs, they're able to get high school jobs based on that. But when you start disrespecting everybody else except the superstar, then it devalues the whole thing. And that's why you see, I think that's why AAU is suffering, I think that's why all of these hoops are suffering because the superstars are not going back, they're creating camps and charging kids $400, $500 to go. So the inner city kids that the guys that's going to go back there and really help, the Genero Pargos, the Kwame Browns, those guys are the ones that's going to impact the kids.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James is a marketing machine, not an individual player
quotes.excerpt: LeBron James is a machine, it's a marketing machine, he's not an individual.
quotes.quote: I thought LeBron James was a regular individual and then I realized he's a part of a group. LeBron James is a machine, it's a marketing machine, he's not an individual. And so, once I realized that, when you go up against a machine, it gives off toxic waste. So what makes it look good, it destroys things around it. And if you look at the careers that he's destroyed, Westbrook, Oladipo before he even started, you got Dalton Knecht because of his son, he didn't get a chance to develop. And he comes there with Andrew Wiggins as the number one draft pick, they make up stories about him to trade him for Kevin Love. It's just like I know what that's like and when I see him go places, I'm like, okay, I want to know which player is going to have to be taken away from for this machine to still look like what it is.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Joel Embiid's success is tied to the 76ers' championship hopes
quotes.excerpt: If Embiid doesn't play 70 games or 65 games and they don't win the championship, it's going to be Joel Embiid.
quotes.quote: We know now it's Joel Embiid. If Embiid doesn't play 70 games or 65 games and they don't win the championship, it's going to be Joel Embiid. If Embiid doesn't play 70 games or 65 games and they don't win the championship, it's going to be Joel Embiid.

quotes.speaker: Host
quotes.summary_phrase: Max Kellerman and Rich Paul's conflicting narratives on Joel Embiid
quotes.excerpt: To me, it automatically came off as bad cop, good cop, set up specifically to be framed like that.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: You got Max Kellerman with him. And there was a recent show which I made a video on, and you had Max Kellerman saying that he heard from somebody that Joel Embiid is a lazy guy and he doesn't really want to work. And then you had Rich Paul saying, no, no, no, that's not true, whatever. To me, it automatically came off as bad cop, good cop, set up specifically to be framed like that, that the narrative gets out from Max Kellerman, but Rich Paul and LeBron James is safe because Rich Paul looks like he's denying it.

text_blocks.speaker: Kwame Brown
text_blocks.text: Rich Paul told him to say it. First of all, what is an agent that has that much influence in the league talking basketball and giving strategic strategies to other people's clients?

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James controls the narrative to avoid taking responsibility
quotes.excerpt: He's trying to control the narrative. And like I said, I used to think he was an individual.
quotes.quote: He's trying to control the narrative. And like I said, I used to think he was an individual. I really liked LeBron James because he's out of high school, and as he go, I go, because it makes the case that it doesn't matter if a kid is out of high school or not, because the top three players, Michael, Kobe, and LeBron, two of those players is right out of high school. So, you know, let's not force people to do things. Some people are ready for opportunities that others are not.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James does not belong in the top three all-time
quotes.excerpt: I see his longevity got him the numbers, but in big moments, I see him as regular.
quotes.quote: I don't see LeBron James in that category. I see his longevity got him the numbers, but in big moments, I see him as regular. Like LeBron James can shy away from the moment at times, and I've never seen Kobe or Michael shy away from that moment. They are built for that. And it's different levels to when that popcorn start popping.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Bryant and Michael Jordan never shied away from moments
quotes.excerpt: I've never seen Kobe or Michael shy away from that moment. They are built for that.
quotes.quote: I've never seen Kobe or Michael shy away from that moment. They are built for that. And it's different levels to when that popcorn start popping. And then, that level of getting to that free throw line while all eyes on you, I mean, I wouldn't personally, I don't think I'm at that level. So I'm not speaking from a guy that's saying, oh, I'm over LeBron James, but it's not many guys are ready for that moment. The whole world is watching you, and it's almost like the kicker at that point. We only hear to see you making, and if you miss, everybody hates you.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Bryant's philosophy on willing a team to a win
quotes.excerpt: You have to find your way to will yourself to a win. Kobe would always say that.
quotes.quote: You have to find your way to will yourself to a win. Kobe would always say that. You have to will that win. Are there going to be occasions where they do such a great job on defense that you have to pass the ball? Yes. But there's times that LeBron will drive right into trouble so that he can have to pass the ball, when he's 6'9". Take that one dribble and pull up, who's going to be there? And that's why MJ and Kobe always worked on that one dribble pull-up, one dribble, two dribble pump fake, so that they can rise up over their guy. And nobody could guard MJ or Kobe.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Bryant and Michael Jordan were superior defenders to LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: MJ would have just turned and shot over him. He wouldn't have got a chance to use his hands.
quotes.quote: You put Ruben Patterson on MJ or Kobe, it would be the worst thing you could have ever done. And I watched them do that to LeBron and I was stunned like, you got Jason Kidd on LeBron? You got Ruben Patterson? And now Jason Kidd got great hands. But MJ would have just turned and shot over him. He wouldn't have got a chance to use his hands because Kobe too. But he's definitely a better defender than Ruben Patterson. Ruben Patterson was able to guard LeBron James and that's crazy.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' decision to not extend LeBron James' son
quotes.excerpt: They realized it was probably going to be way, I mean, he's a big guy.
quotes.quote: Because they realized it was probably going to be way, I mean, he's a big guy, but once people figured out that he couldn't shoot that jump shot consistently, he would have been easier to guard with that hand check, because you can back up off him and you can get a hold of him easy with his hip. But when you take that hand check away with a guy that size and that fast, going in the full court, I mean, he almost had to get out of his way because when they took the hand check away and added in freedom of movement, anytime they got into you and bumped you, it was a foul call. So it was almost like we went from real basketball to where we meet force with force, to it was almost like when force is coming, we got to avoid it, we got to get out of the way. So it made it almost impossible to play defense, so I realized they were trying to gear the game towards scoring, which the fans wanted to see.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' age affects his ability to close games
quotes.excerpt: They don't understand he's 42 years old and he can't close anymore.
quotes.quote: The media and the LeBron fans don't want to believe that, but they don't understand he's 42 years old and he can't close anymore. So, I mean, all he's going to do is come there and make one of your young and up-and-coming players, you're going to delay their development, and that's it.

quotes.speaker: Kwame Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' career feels scripted for legacy purposes
quotes.excerpt: LeBron's James career looks kind of scripted a lot of times, like this has to be done.
quotes.quote: LeBron's James career looks kind of scripted a lot of times, like this has to be done so this shows up well in his career. This has to be done and so on. And I think part of it, I have nothing completely nothing against the kid and against this kid Bronny, nothing. I don't know the guy, but just speaking basketball wise, I think it was more made that he was drafted more made for LeBron's legacy because he can't catch like Mike or Kobe in certain things, but he can say, listen, I'm the only father-son duo that was on the basketball court. I'm the only father-son duo that was in the playoffs. And now it's going to be the only father-son duo that goes against each other. So you're going to have Bronny defending LeBron James and making a huge deal out of it. I think it's all just done on purpose. It certainly looks like it to me, I don't know.
